note: Arterial tortuosity is established as a key hallmark of Loeys-Dietz syndrome (including SMAD2-related LDS6) that distinguishes it from Marfan syndrome.

evidence.text: Loeys-Dietz syndrome is characterized by a multisystemic triad including aortic aneurysm with arterial tortuosity, with SMAD2 identified among the causative TGF-beta pathway genes.

source.title: Loeys-dietz syndrome
source.quote: The most typical clinical triad includes hypertelorism, bifid uvula or cleft palate and aortic aneurysm with tortuosity... The genetic cause is heterogeneous and includes mutations in genes encoding for components of the transforming growth factor beta (TGFβ) signalling pathway: TGFBR1, TGFBR2, SMAD2, SMAD3, TGFB2 and TGFB3.

evidence.text: Loeys-Dietz syndrome phenotypically resembles Marfan syndrome, but LDS patients uniquely exhibit widespread arterial tortuosity.
